html:
Nkore, later called Ankole, was a kingdom in south-western Uganda, east of Lake Edward, from about the 1400s to 1967. The map shows it in its 1815 snapshot.

It was a land of cattle. Its ruler, the mugabe, came from the Bahima, herders of the famous long-horned Ankole cattle, while most people were Bairu farmers who paid them tribute. Nkore was one of several Great Lakes kingdoms, and it fought for land and cattle with Bunyoro to the north and with Rwanda to the south.

In 1901 its chiefs signed an agreement with the British that made it part of the Uganda Protectorate, and its borders grew under British rule. In 1967 President Milton Obote abolished Uganda's kingdoms. Unlike Buganda, Ankole was not restored in the 1990s.
